cands.bio: Republican member of the Alabama State Senate for District 17 since November 2014. Earned a business finance degree and a math M.A.Ed. at the University of Montevallo. Worked as a high school teacher and coach, taught at Jefferson State Community College, and worked in real estate and business development.
cands.gaps: We found no stated positions from him on data centers, development or growth, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, policing, or school choice and teacher pay. His only issue statements in the pages we read are from his 2014 campaign website, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's 2022 or 2026 candidate surveys. We found no 2026 campaign platform and no endorsements for this election. His birthplace, where he grew up, and when he came to Alabama are not stated in the pages we read; only his birth date (September 21, 1967) appears. We found no documented controversies and no foreign ties.

qual.background: State senator since 2014 (about 12 years), including service on the Finance and Taxation General Fund committee and as Banking and Insurance chair. Earlier worked as a teacher and coach, a college instructor, and in real estate and business development. Holds a business finance degree.
qual.why: More than a decade of legislative service plus a finance degree and business and real estate experience puts him in the high band. The committee chairmanship was not counted.

pro-life.evidence: Voted in May 2019 to make abortion a crime at any stage of pregnancy, with no exemptions for rape or incest (as reported by Wikipedia; no roll call was opened).

second-amendment.evidence: In his 2014 campaign site statement he said he is an NRA and Gun Owners of America member and 'will always oppose restrictions on our constitutional rights' to bear arms.
